Allcargo Terminals records nearly two-fold rise in September-quarter profit
#Warehousing & Logistics#Industrial#India
Last Updated : 10 Nov 2026
Share
Font size
ABC Small
ABCMedium
ABCLarge
Print
Comment
Synopsis
Logistics operator Allcargo Terminals Ltd has reported a consolidated profit after tax of INR 21 crore for the September quarter, almost double the INR 11 crore recorded in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 21.5 per cent to INR 252 crore from INR 207 crore, driven by higher volumes across the company's container freight station and inland container depot network. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation grew 45.9 per cent to INR 59 crore, which the company attributed to cost discipline, process optimisation and better asset utilisation across its pan-India logistics terminal operations.
‹›
Representative image
Logistics operator Allcargo Terminals Ltd on Wednesday reported a consolidated profit after tax of INR 21 crore for the September quarter, against INR 11 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue for the period stood at INR 252 crore, up 21.5 per cent from INR 207 crore recorded during the July-September period of the preceding financial year, the company said in a statement. Allcargo Terminals said the revenue growth was driven by higher volumes across its pan-India container freight station and inland container depot network.
The company delivered earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation of INR 59 crore during the September quarter, compared with INR 40 crore in the second quarter of the previous financial year, growing 45.9 per cent year-on-year. The company said this reflected continued focus on cost discipline, process optimisation and better asset utilisation.
Allcargo Terminals Managing Director Pranav Choudhary said the growth reflected continued progress in the business, supported by focused yield management, increased transhipment activity and the strength of the company's operational network. He said the company's focus remained on driving operational efficiencies, optimising business opportunities across its container freight station and inland container depot network, and strengthening capabilities to support India's evolving import-export trade requirements.
Container freight stations and inland container depots serve as logistics nodes that handle customs clearance, storage and onward movement of containerised cargo between ports and inland destinations, forming an important part of India's trade infrastructure. Operators in this segment have benefited in recent years from steady growth in India's containerised trade volumes, as manufacturers and exporters increasingly rely on organised logistics infrastructure to manage customs compliance and reduce transit times between ports and inland industrial clusters.
The company's pan-India network allows it to serve exporters and importers across multiple industrial corridors, with transhipment activity, the movement of cargo between vessels or modes of transport at intermediate points, cited as a contributor to the quarter's earnings growth. Industry analysts tracking India's logistics infrastructure sector have said that container freight station and inland container depot operators with wider geographic coverage have generally been better positioned to capture incremental volume growth as India's export base diversifies across more manufacturing clusters beyond the traditional port-adjacent industrial belts.
The improvement in both revenue and profitability during the quarter adds to a broader pattern of steady performance among listed logistics infrastructure operators in India, even as overall economic growth and trade volumes have shown some variability through the year.
Source PTI
